name_evidence.source: southaustralia.com/products/fleurieu-peninsula/destination-information/yankalilla destination page; the Normanville-Carrickalinga-Second Valley-Rapid Bay coast (Yankalilla district)
name_evidence.wording: Yankalilla destination page names the Yankalilla District Historical Museum, Christ Church (1857, Shrine of Our Lady of Yankalilla) and a heritage trail. Weakest name of the four: the alternative is to place these as spots of Victor Harbor or leave them standalone; the town is folded into the destination and Cape Jervis, Deep Creek and the coast between are its spots.

spots.bio: A wine region and town on the plains east of the Fleurieu hills.
spots.name: Langhorne Creek
spots.note: A wine region named by Wikivoyage (one of four on the peninsula), the board and southaustralia.com, not a single cellar door; keep the region/town, individual wineries rejected.

spots.bio: A migratory wader birdwatching site on Lake Alexandrina, with a lookout and picnic area.
spots.name: Tolderol Game Reserve
spots.note: southaustralia.com and Parks SA: well-known migratory wader birdwatching site on Lake Alexandrina, lookout and picnic area, wetlands reopened Aug 2025 (note: seasonal best Sep-Mar, short duck-hunting season).

spots.bio: A family animal park in Goolwa with feeding and animal encounters.
spots.name: Animal Farm
spots.note: Open family animal park in Goolwa, named by the board's tours and wildlife-encounters pages; feeding and animal encounters fill an hour or more.

spots.bio: A century-old family garage turned museum in 2019, with Buicks, Holdens and motorbikes.
spots.name: Gilbert's Motor Museum
spots.note: Board heritage page calls it a must for motoring enthusiasts: century-old family garage turned museum in 2019 with Buicks, Holdens and bikes; open to the public.

spots.bio: A small museum of locally made South Australian cars at 45 Gardiner St.
spots.name: Goolwa Motor Museum
spots.note: Wikivoyage Goolwa See lists this small museum of locally made SA cars at 45 Gardiner St; a different museum in a different town from Gilbert's. Small, but a guide names it.

spots.bio: A local history museum in Strathalbyn with interactive displays, suited to a half-hour visit.
spots.name: Strathalbyn Districts Museum and Heritage Centre
spots.note: Local history museum in Strathalbyn named by the board's heritage and arts pages; interactive displays suit a half-hour visit in a heritage town.

spots.bio: A national park on the Southern Ocean coast and the start of the Heysen Trail, with Tapanappa and Blowhole Beach.
spots.name: Deep Creek National Park

spots.bio: The Kangaroo Island ferry terminal and the start of the Heysen Trail, at the tip of the peninsula.
spots.name: Cape Jervis

spots.bio: The multi-day coastal walk from Cape Jervis to Victor Harbor, a section of the Heysen Trail.
spots.name: Wild South Coast Way
spots.note: Rule 1-2: board and Heysen Trail pages name the Cape Jervis to Victor Harbor coastal walk (Wild South Coast Way) as a multi-day walk, like Hump Ridge Track; a distinct walk.

spots.bio: A protected bay with a jetty and boat sheds, known for snorkelling and for leafy sea dragons.
spots.name: Second Valley
spots.note: Rule 1-2: board lists it twice; sheltered cove known for snorkelling, cliff jumping and its jetty, a recognised Fleurieu stop.

spots.bio: A long beach below the town of Normanville with a picnic area.
spots.name: Normanville
spots.note: Rule 1: board and southaustralia.com name it; long beach below Normanville with picnic area, second-tier stop.

spots.bio: A beach village with white sand and rock pools, in an International Dark Sky Community.
spots.name: Carrickalinga
spots.note: Beach village the regional board singles out (white-sand beach, rock pools, International Dark Sky Community): second-tier beach stop.
